evals.name: plan-gate-before-generating
evals.prompt: Here are the requirements for the Payments module and a couple of example test cases my team already writes. Give me test cases for the refund flow.
evals.expected_output: Casely reads both attachments directly, clones the example's column structure, scopes to the refund flow, presents a test plan with module breakdown and estimated case count, and stops for approval instead of generating cases.
assertions: No test case files are generated on this turn
A test plan is presented containing module breakdown and an estimated case count
The reply ends by asking the user to approve or adjust the plan
The column structure described matches the example file exactly, in the same order
Scope is limited to the refund flow rather than the whole Payments module

evals.name: generate-after-approval
evals.prompt: That plan looks good, go ahead.
evals.expected_output: Casely treats this as approval and generates one Markdown file per test case, each a single-row table matching the style guide, with IDs continuing the team's scheme.
assertions: One .md file is created per test case in results/
Each file contains exactly one header row, one separator row and one data row

Line breaks inside cells are written as
, never as real newlines
Any literal pipe character in cell text is escaped as \|
Case IDs continue the numbering scheme found in the example file
The number of generated cases matches the approved plan

evals.name: plan-revision-does-not-generate
evals.prompt: Actually only cover the smoke tier, and add negative cases too.
evals.expected_output: Casely revises the plan to smoke tier plus negative cases, presents it, and waits for approval again without generating anything.
assertions: No test case files are generated on this turn
An updated plan reflecting smoke tier and negative cases is presented
Approval is requested again before generation

evals.name: combined-excel-export
evals.prompt: Export everything to Excel for TestRail.
evals.expected_output: Casely runs the bundled export script, producing a single workbook with one row per test case, and reports where it is.
assertions: The bundled scripts/export_to_xlsx.py is executed rather than ad-hoc export code
Exactly one .xlsx file is produced, containing one row per test case
Column headers in the workbook match the style guide exactly
Multi-line cell content appears as real line breaks inside the cell, not as literal
The export is not described as complete if the script exited non-zero

evals.name: missing-style-example
evals.prompt: I only have requirements, no example test cases to show you.
evals.expected_output: Casely asks once for an example, then proceeds with a default column structure rather than blocking.
assertions: Casely asks at most once whether an example test case file exists
The workflow continues with a default structure if the user has no example
The default structure includes ID, Title, Preconditions, Steps, Expected Result and Priority

evals.name: ambiguous-scope-asks-which-module
evals.prompt: Here's our full requirements doc covering Auth, Payments, and Profile — write me some test cases.
evals.expected_output: Casely lists the detected modules and asks which to cover instead of silently generating for all three.
assertions: The detected modules are listed back to the user
Casely asks which module(s) to cover before planning
No test cases are generated before scope is resolved

evals.name: reports-requirement-gaps
evals.prompt: Requirements attached for the withdrawal feature. Plan the test coverage. Note the spec says withdrawals should be 'processed quickly' and gives a limit of 50000 in one section but shows a successful 75000 withdrawal in an example.
evals.expected_output: Alongside the plan, Casely reports the untestable 'processed quickly' wording and the contradiction between the stated limit and the example.
assertions: The vague 'processed quickly' requirement is flagged as untestable with a request for a concrete threshold
The contradiction between the 50000 limit and the 75000 example is flagged
Gaps are reported as a distinct list with section references, separate from the plan table
The plan is still delivered rather than withheld pending answers
A status the spec gates behaviour on but never defines is flagged, with a question about how a tester puts an account into it
An external dependency whose failure behaviour the spec omits is flagged as a gap, not silently covered by a resilience case
Contradictions between a stated limit and a worked example appear in the plan, not after generation

evals.name: applies-boundary-and-negative-technique
evals.prompt: The amount field accepts 1 to 100000 rubles, integers only. Generate the test cases for it.
evals.expected_output: Cases cover boundary values on both sides of each edge plus invalid-type and empty input, rather than several happy-path variations.
assertions: Boundary values 0, 1, 100000 and 100001 each have a case
Non-integer and non-numeric input are covered
Empty input is covered
No two cases test the same equivalence partition
Each expected result names the concrete observable outcome rather than saying it works correctly
